title: ED attachment of property bought before the crime

scenes.dialogue: Can the Enforcement Directorate attach property you bought years before the alleged crime even happened, so it was never bought with crime money?
The Kerala High Court has said no, unless the proceeds went abroad. The Delhi High Court took a wider view. So which view would the Karnataka High Court take?
Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On twenty eighth October, twenty twenty six, Honourable Justice Suraj Govindaraj of the Karnataka High Court ruled.
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On 28 October 2026, Honourable Justice Suraj Govindaraj of the Karnataka High Court ruled.

scenes.dialogue: The petitioner bought a flat in two thousand four and some land in two thousand eight. The alleged offence, over iron ore, is from twenty eleven and twelve.
scenes.shown: The petitioner bought a flat in 2004 and some land in 2008. The alleged offence, over iron ore, is from 2011-12.

scenes.dialogue: In twenty twenty four, the E D provisionally attached both. It did not claim they were bought with crime money, but held them as property of equal value.
scenes.shown: In 2024, the ED provisionally attached both. It did not claim they were bought with crime money, but held them as property of equal value.

scenes.dialogue: His counsel argued that property bought before a crime can never be its proceeds, and that equal value property can be taken only when proceeds go abroad.
The E D said the original money had been withdrawn or moved on, and that the petition was premature, as the Act has its own remedies.
scenes.shown: The ED said the original money had been withdrawn or moved on, and that the petition was premature, as the Act has its own remedies.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? Property bought before the crime can still be attached for equal value, if the Act's conditions are met, even with nothing abroad.
Whether those conditions are met is for the Adjudicating Authority, on the merits. So the writ petition was dismissed, with all remedies left open.
